Executive Summary:
Upon further investigation, suspicious network connection was observed from "chrome.exe" on device "ejwin10pf3dw4dw". The process tree shows "chrome.exe" was launched from the folder path: "C:\Program Files\Google\Chrome\Application". "chrome.exe" is a legitimate signed browser process by Google LLC and typically used for web browsing. Multiple outbound connections were made to various domains, including several legitimate ones such as google[.]com, translate[.]google[.]co[.]uk, and figma[.]com. However, connection attempts to "reknitless[.]com" were blocked several times by network protection as potential command-and-control (C2) activity. These actions were identified as "ExploitGuardNetworkProtectionBlocked", confirming that security controls effectively prevented the suspicious activity. No evidence of persistence mechanisms or registry modifications was found, and no files were quarantined during this event. The observed activity includes hands-on-keyboard signals and pre-ransom logic indicators typically associated with human-operated attack attempts, but no further malicious process executions were detected. This activity likely seems from general browsing, where the user may have visited ad networks, infected sites, or parked domains. The network protection feature successfully blocked the connection, and no further action is required. Therefore, we are resolving this incident.
